_comment: The judging set for any new conflation detector. Drawn 2026-09-26
BEFORE the redesign started, by scripts/draw_conflation_judge_set.py.
PROTOCOL, fixed now so it cannot be bent to fit a result:
1. Design uses conflation_labels.json only. Nobody opens these records
until the new detector is frozen in a commit.
2. Label the first block in `order`, from titles, years and per-paper
institutions, with no detector score (old or new) on screen.
Labels: conflated, one_person, unsure, not_a_person -- the same
meanings as conflation_labels.json.
3. If fewer than 10 are conflated, label the next 40 in order, and
repeat until 10 are or the order runs out. The stopping rule reads
only the labels, never a detector.
4. Score the deployed detector and the frozen new one ONCE each.
5. ADOPT the new one only if, on this set, it (a) finds more of the
conflated records than the deployed one, (b) at least 30% of what
it flags here is conflated, and (c) it flags no more than 20% of
the living people with six or more papers -- a queue a person can
actually read.
6. Anything changed after step 4 is marked tuned, and its figures on
this set are no longer evidence.
LABELLED 2026-09-26, positions 0-119, from blind cards (titles, years, the
author's own per-paper institutions), with no detector score computed for any
of them: 11 conflated, 106 one_person, 3 unsure. Ten or more conflated, so by
step 3 no extension was drawn. Committed before step 4 was run.
CAVEAT, known before scoring: per-paper institutions were on the cards, and the
new detector reads institutions too. Where a label leaned on an institution
(an SGPGI paper on a PGIMER record, a Schneider Electric paper on a Bristol
statistician), the subject matter differed as well; no label rests on an
institution alone.
JUDGED 2026-09-26, once, as step 4 says: see `judged`. The new detector met all three criteria and is the default.
population: living people with >= 6 papers and no label

QUESTION: should rip.conflation.FOREIGN_REPORT_AT be 1 instead of 2, i.e.
report a single paper foreign only at subfield level? On round 1 that
would have found 8 of 11 instead of 4, but it was seen after scoring,
so round 1 is now design data for this question and cannot judge it.
PROTOCOL:
1. Label positions 120-239 of `order` exactly as round 1: blind cards
(titles, years, the author's own institutions), no score computed.
2. If fewer than 10 are conflated, label the next 40, and repeat.
3. Commit the labels. Then score FOREIGN_REPORT_AT = 2 (deployed) and 1
once each, everything else identical, on one snapshot.
4. ADOPT 1 only if, on these labels: (a) it finds more conflated records
than 2; (b) at least 30% of what it flags here is conflated; (c) it
flags no more than 20% of living people with six or more papers; (d)
if 3 or more records here are flagged by 1 and not by 2, at least
20% of those are conflated.
5. Anything changed after step 3 is marked tuned.
LABELLED 2026-09-27, positions 120-239, blind, before any score: 17 conflated,
101 one_person, 2 unsure. Ten or more conflated, so no extension.
JUDGED 2026-09-27, once: all four criteria met; see `judged`.

_comment: Fixed 2026-09-29, before any record at these positions was opened and before
any design work on the question.
QUESTION: can the detector see people whose papers carry no topic in
OpenAlex's taxonomy (27% of people with six or more papers)? Candidate: infer
a paper's OpenAlex field from its title, using the corpus's own OpenAlex-placed
papers as training data, and apply the existing foreign-work rule to the
inferred subjects of records that have no placed topic at all.
PROTOCOL:
1. Design uses conflation_labels.json and rounds 1 and 2 only. The candidate
is frozen in a commit before any round-3 record is opened.
2. Label ALL remaining positions, 240-366 (127 records, 36 of them with no
placed topic), blind, exactly as rounds 1 and 2. There is nothing left to
extend with, so no stopping rule.
3. Commit the labels. Then score the current default and the candidate once
each on one snapshot.
4. ADOPT only if, on these labels: (a) the candidate finds at least one more
conflated record than the current default; (b) of the records only the
candidate flags, at least 30% are conflated; (c) at least 30% of all it
flags here are conflated; (d) it flags no more than 20% of living people
with six or more papers.
5. Anything changed after step 3 is marked tuned. With perhaps five to eight
conflations among the 36 blind records, this can reject a bad signal but
can only weakly confirm a good one; the report must say so.
